scenes.audio: The Oreo you are eating today is fake, because the real Oreo closed down in 1999.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: A young man (early 20s, tan skin, messy dark hair, cream-colored t-shirt with a colorful rickshaw print) holds a blue Oreo pack directly in front of his face. He slowly lowers the pack to reveal his face. Lighting is soft from the front, with a cool blue background glow.

scenes.audio: Let me tell you how. Look, once upon a time, there were two brothers, Jacob and Joseph.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: The man gestures with his hand, explaining. Behind him is a studio setting with monitors and acoustic foam panels. Handheld camera movement creates a slight shake.

scenes.audio: Both were owners of a big bakery. But one day, a fight broke out between them.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: 2D Animation: Two figures representing Jacob (with mustache and glasses) and Joseph appear on a pink background with '1890s' text. A bakery storefront illustration appears between them, labeled 'Bakery' in Kansas City, Missouri.

scenes.audio: Joseph said, 'Brother, I will grow this bakery by partnering up.'
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Live-action stock footage: Two men in business suits (one South Asian, one East Asian) are arguing heatedly in a modern office hallway. The South Asian man gestures emphatically with his hands.

scenes.audio: Jacob said, 'You'll get a slap!' I mean, he had other plans.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The man from Scene 1 returns, acting out the dialogue. He looks to the side to represent Joseph, then looks back to the camera to represent Jacob's reaction, gesturing with a dismissive hand movement.

scenes.audio: So things didn't work out between them, and Jacob left the bakery.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: B&W cinematic shot: A man in a dark jacket sits in shadows, head down, looking distressed. Harsh side lighting creates deep shadows.

scenes.audio: And he started something of his own. Meanwhile, Joseph made his bakery even bigger.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: 2D Animation: A bald cartoon character with glasses and a mustache (Jacob) is in a kitchen. The scene cuts to Joseph with partners laughing in front of a large brick building labeled 'Nabisco'.

scenes.audio: But during that time, on the other side, Jacob made a biscuit named Hydrox.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: 2D Animation: Jacob holds up a dark chocolate sandwich cookie. A radial sunburst background highlights the cookie as it spins.

scenes.audio: And as soon as this biscuit launched, people went crazy for it.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Archival footage: Vintage print advertisements for Hydrox cookies showing piles of biscuits and a child eating one.

scenes.audio: Because they had never eaten such a biscuit before...
scenes.label: Real Experience
scenes.visual: Stock footage: A woman with dark hair tied back sits at a white desk, looking at a laptop with a shocked facial expression, hands to her face.

scenes.audio: ...which had cream in the middle. So these biscuits sold rapidly.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: The man from Scene 1 uses his hands to mimic the layers of a sandwich cookie. Cut to stock footage of an older woman with grey hair in a kitchen, talking on the phone and writing in a notebook.

scenes.label: Real Experience
scenes.visual: Stock footage: A man with a beard and glasses wearing a striped shirt and apron looks at a blue tablet and smiles widely.

scenes.audio: But Joseph was watching this. So he copied Hydrox and created Oreo.
scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.visual: Stock footage: A man looks out a window with a serious, envious expression. Cut to 2D animation of Joseph looking sad, then holding up an Oreo cookie that he just created.

scenes.audio: Now what happened was, the name 'Hydrox' sounded like something used to clean a bathroom or toilet.
scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.visual: Split screen/collage: A Hydrox cookie is shown. Cut to stock footage of someone in pink gloves spraying cleaning fluid, then a person in a white hazmat suit cleaning a toilet.

scenes.audio: So people stopped buying it after Oreo arrived. And then everyone thought Hydrox was a copy of Oreo.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Graphic transition: A Hydrox cookie morphs into an Oreo cookie. Packs of both are shown side-by-side on a blue background. The video ends with a plate of Oreos under a large logo.
